features.name: Home page and main feature navigation
steps: Enter PLAY, SELECT LEVEL, RANDOM PUZZLE, MULTIPLAYER, HOW TO PLAY, and SETTINGS respectively
features.expected: The positions of the home entries, the back behavior, and the current Level state; progress must not be reset abnormally when switching between pages

features.name: Fixed-level selection and lock state
steps: Enter SELECT LEVEL for the first time
Only unlocked levels may be entered
Tapping a locked level must not start it directly
features.expected: The level lock state is persistent state; in the initial screenshot Level 1 is enterable while the other levels are locked; after completing Level 1 it must correctly advance to Level 2 rather than unlocking all levels at once

features.name: Basic Nonogram board rules and Fill / Cross operations
steps: Determine cells from the left row hints and the top column hints
Select FILL and then tap a cell to fill
Mark the cells known to be empty
Keep operating until the correct picture is formed
features.expected: Core business logic. Each row/column hint represents a run of filled cells; multiple numbers represent multiple independent runs. Three states must be maintained: undetermined / Fill / Cross; Cross must not be treated as filled.

features.name: Board-clue and completion-condition validation
steps: Fill the corresponding runs in a row or column according to the clues
Deliberately leave missing cells, extra fills, or wrong positions
The whole puzzle must not be judged complete
features.expected: It must not merely check "how many cells are filled"; the entire final answer must be validated; the row/column constraints and the final hidden picture should be consistent; a wrong layout must not pass even with the same total fill count

features.name: Operation-mode and cell-state switching
steps: Use Fill / Cross repeatedly on the same puzzle
After enabling LONG PRESS TO CROSS, long-press a cell to test Cross
After enabling CYCLE MODE test the cyclic switching of a single cell's state
Re-verify the operation mode is restored after closing the settings
features.expected: The setting must genuinely change the board input logic rather than only toggling the UI; a mode change must not damage the existing board state

features.name: Undo, Hint, and Restart
steps: Operate several consecutive steps on the board
Tap UNDO to step back the most recent operation
Use HINT to get a valid hint/correct state
The board returns to the initial puzzle
features.expected: Undo steps back through the operation history in reverse; the Hint result must match the real answer; Restart clears the user's operations while keeping the current puzzle, difficulty, and clues; the timer/move reset behavior should also be consistent

features.name: Timer and Moves state
steps: Observe the TIME and MOVES at the top
Continue operating after Undo, Hint, and Restart
features.expected: The timer keeps counting from the game start; Moves changes with the actual operations; the completion screen should show the final MOVES and TIME consistent with the gameplay

features.name: Full completion flow for the fixed levels
steps: Show the picture, Moves, and Time
features.expected: This is the main fixed-level E2E. After completion the completion state must be recorded and the next level unlocked; the screenshots confirm that both Level 1 and Level 2 have independent completion pictures and statistics

features.name: The completion result and the return path
steps: Verify the hidden picture, move count, and time in the completion dialog
Tap NEXT LEVEL to enter the next level; after another completion choose HOME
features.expected: The NEXT LEVEL and HOME paths must have consistent states; a completed level must not be lost by returning home; BUY ME A COFFEE is an auxiliary entry and not a core benchmark feature

features.name: Random Puzzle five-difficulty selection
steps: Select Easy, Medium, Hard, Master, and Expert respectively
Generate the corresponding random Nonogram each time
features.expected: All five difficulties must exist. Difficulty changes should genuinely affect the generated puzzle rather than only the title; the current random puzzle's difficulty, clues, and answer state should be saved

features.name: Random Nonogram generation logic
steps: Generate several Random Puzzles in a row at the same difficulty
Compare the board answer with the row/column clues
features.expected: One of the reproduction's key points. Generation must first produce a valid answer grid and then correctly compute all row/column run clues from that answer; the generated result must reach a legal completed state from the displayed clues and must not generate a board inconsistent with the clues

features.name: Full puzzle solving on Expert, the highest difficulty
steps: Keep filling/crossing according to complex multi-run row/column clues
features.expected: The highest-value reasoning task. The screenshot shows that Expert already uses a 12×12 board with many multi-run row/column clues such as 2 3 1 2 and 1 3 1 1; continuous cross-row/column constraint propagation with many intermediate states and global consistency is required

features.name: Random-puzzle behavior consistency across difficulties
steps: Complete puzzles on Easy / Medium / Hard / Master / Expert respectively
Check that all five difficulties use the same base rules, completion detection, Moves, Timer, Hint, and Restart
Compare the puzzle complexity across the difficulty levels
features.expected: The core rules must be unified across all difficulties; difficulty may only change generation parameters such as puzzle size and complexity and must not cause rule inconsistencies; in particular Expert must be verified not to be merely a scaled-up UI

features.name: How To Play tutorial
steps: Browse the 4 rule modules: Reveal the Picture
features.expected: Correctly display Fill, blank/X, row/column clues, and the completion goal; the tutorial page's layout, icons, text hierarchy, and scroll state are part of the visual reproduction requirements

features.name: Settings basic game settings
steps: Toggle HAPTIC FEEDBACK, LONG PRESS TO CROSS, and CYCLE MODE
Actually perform the corresponding input operations
Then enter the settings to confirm the state
features.expected: The settings must persist; Haptic corresponds to touch feedback; Long Press and Cycle Mode must genuinely affect board input behavior rather than being static switches

features.name: Reset Progress global progress reset
steps: First complete at least two fixed levels
Confirm that the next level is unlocked
Return to the home page and Select Level
features.expected: The fixed levels' completion/unlock progress should be cleared and the initial Level state restored; unrelated states such as app settings and random toggles must not be wrongly cleared at the same time, unless the target app's observable behavior is such

features.name: Mid-way exit and level-state restoration
steps: Return to the previous page or Home
Enter PLAY / the corresponding level again
Check the puzzle and progress state
features.expected: Test the lifecycle and state persistence. It must be implemented correctly according to the actual app's behavior
